brief.meaningEn: Become less appealing after an initially attractive period.
brief.meaningZh: 原本吸引人的事物逐漸失去吸引力。
brief.grammar: Lose/loses/lost + possessive + charm; the possessive refers to the thing becoming less attractive.
brief.register: Everyday consumer advice: a parent explains to another parent why novelty alone is a weak reason to buy a toy.
brief.boundaryZh: 失去吸引力不等於產品已損壞，也不表示每個人都不再喜歡。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只因某物舊了便斷定它失去吸引力；要有興趣轉淡的證據。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨新鮮感消退、實際損壞與仍然有用。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 75, row 10; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Cheap gadgets often lose their charm quickly.

listening.en: The flashing toy thrilled Mei on Monday, but by Friday she ignored it although it still worked. Such gadgets can lose their charm quickly.
listening.zh: 閃燈玩具星期一令美很興奮，到星期五她已不理會它，雖然玩具仍能使用。這類玩具很快就會失去吸引力。
listening.promptZh: lose their charm 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: They become less appealing after the initial excitement fades.
options.zh: 最初的興奮消退後，它們變得沒那麼吸引。

options.en: They stop working mechanically by Friday.
options.zh: 它們到星期五便機械故障。

options.en: Mei has never liked any flashing toy.
options.zh: 美從來不喜歡任何閃燈玩具。

options.en: Their price must have fallen.
options.zh: 它們的價錢一定下降了。

listening.explanationZh: 玩具仍能使用，但美的興趣已轉淡。

reply.promptEn: Why is the new puzzle no longer on the café table? Customers tried it often during its first week, but hardly anyone chooses it now; all pieces are intact.
reply.promptZh: （為何咖啡室桌上不再放那款新拼圖？首星期客人經常玩，現在幾乎沒有人選它；所有拼圖塊仍齊全。）

options.en: Customers seem less interested in the puzzle now.
options.zh: 客人現在似乎對拼圖較沒興趣。

options.en: The initial novelty has faded despite the intact pieces.
options.zh: 即使拼圖塊齊全，最初的新鮮感仍已消退。

options.en: The puzzle has lost its charm for many customers.
options.zh: 對許多客人而言，拼圖已失去吸引力。

options.en: Its condition is sound, but demand has weakened.
options.zh: 它仍完好，但受歡迎程度下降。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均根據使用量下降而非損壞作答；金句用 lost its charm。

scene.promptZh: 展覽開幕時有長龍；三個月後展品仍完好，回頭客卻明顯減少。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The display may have lost its charm for repeat visitors.
options.zh: 對回頭客而言，展覽可能已失去吸引力。

options.en: The display has definitely been damaged.
options.zh: 展覽一定已損壞。

options.en: Nobody enjoyed the exhibition at its opening.
options.zh: 開幕時沒有人喜歡展覽。

scene.explanationZh: 回頭客減少支持吸引力下降，不能推出展品損壞。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以支持 lose its charm？

options.en: Visitors came back less often after their first enthusiastic month.
options.zh: 訪客首月熱情，之後回訪較少。

options.en: The same readers still choose the old book every week.
options.zh: 同一批讀者每星期仍選那本舊書。

options.en: Children stopped requesting the game although it still works.
options.zh: 遊戲仍可用，但孩子不再要求玩。

contrast.explanationZh: 持續主動選擇，沒有顯示吸引力消退。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「這款玩具失去吸引力，就代表它壞了。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: It can lose its charm while still working perfectly.
options.zh: 它即使仍能正常使用，也可能失去吸引力。

options.en: A working toy must remain exciting forever.
options.zh: 能運作的玩具一定永遠有趣。

options.en: If interest fades, the toy was never appealing.
options.zh: 若興趣消退，玩具起初就一定不吸引。

dialogue.explanationZh: 吸引力和功能是兩個不同判斷。

speaking.en: The app lost its charm for commuters once its daily tips began repeating, although every feature still worked.
speaking.zh: 應用程式的每日提示開始重複後，對通勤者而言失去吸引力，雖然所有功能仍能使用。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出興趣變化和功能狀態。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：校園午餐投票的新介面首週吸引很多學生；一個月後，學生覺得選項總是相同，參與人數下降；系統並沒有故障。用一至兩句英文說明變化，避免誤稱它壞了。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出首週受歡迎、重複選項令參與下降、系統仍能運作。

examples.en: After attracting many students in its first week, the lunch-vote interface lost its charm after a month: repeated choices reduced participation, even though the system still worked.
examples.zh: 午餐投票介面首週吸引很多學生，但一個月後失去吸引力：重複的選項令參與人數下降，儘管系統仍能運作。

examples.en: Although it drew many students in its first week, the interface lost its charm when repeated options made participation fall; there was no technical fault.
examples.zh: 雖然介面首週吸引很多學生，但重複的選項令參與人數下降，它便失去吸引力；系統並沒有技術故障。

takeaways.en: Something can lose its charm when interest fades.
takeaways.zh: 興趣轉淡時，某物可以失去吸引力。

takeaways.en: A toy can lose its charm while still working perfectly.
takeaways.zh: 失去吸引力不一定代表東西損壞。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Something fairly important or impressive, expressed in an informal, understated way.
brief.meaningZh: 一件頗重要或令人印象深刻的事，語氣較口語。
brief.grammar: Be a pretty big deal for/to someone; pretty intensifies big in informal speech, not physical attractiveness.
brief.register: Friendly conversation: a music teacher tells a student that their first public performance matters to them personally without claiming it is world-famous.
brief.boundaryZh: 重要程度可因人而異；不代表全球大事，也不是外表漂亮。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把 pretty 理解為漂亮，亦不要推斷事情對每個人同樣重要。
brief.outcomeZh: 能依說話者和對象判斷個人重要性與語氣。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 76, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The first concert was a pretty big deal for her.

listening.en: Lena has practised alone for years. Playing her first concert for an audience is a pretty big deal for her, even if the hall is small.
listening.zh: 蓮娜獨自練習多年。首次在觀眾面前演出，對她而言是件頗重要的事，即使演奏廳不大。
listening.promptZh: a pretty big deal 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: The first performance matters a lot to Lena personally.
options.zh: 首次演出對蓮娜個人頗重要。

options.en: The concert hall looks physically beautiful.
options.zh: 演奏廳外觀漂亮。

options.en: Every person in the country knows about her concert.
options.zh: 全國每個人都知道她的音樂會。

options.en: The hall must be enormous.
options.zh: 演奏廳一定很大。

listening.explanationZh: 多年練習後首次公開演出，說的是個人重要性。

reply.promptEn: Why does Arun want a photograph of his first published poem? He worked on it for months and is proud, though it appears only in the school magazine.
reply.promptZh: （阿倫為何想為首次發表的詩拍照？他花了幾個月修改，感到自豪，雖然詩只刊於校刊。）

options.en: Publishing the poem matters personally to Arun.
options.zh: 發表這首詩對阿倫個人有意義。

options.en: Months of work make the first publication memorable for him.
options.zh: 幾個月的努力令首次發表值得他紀念。

options.en: His first published poem is a pretty big deal to him.
options.zh: 首次發表詩作對他而言是件頗重要的事。

options.en: He values the achievement despite its modest audience.
options.zh: 即使讀者不多，他仍重視這項成就。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都肯定個人成就而不誇稱全國知名。

scene.promptZh: 阿姨首次完成半馬，雖不是冠軍，仍十分重視。哪句最自然？

options.en: Finishing her first half-marathon is a pretty big deal to her.
options.zh: 首次跑畢半馬對她而言是件頗重要的事。

options.en: She must have won an international title.
options.zh: 她一定奪得國際冠軍。

options.en: Pretty means her running shoes look beautiful.
options.zh: pretty 表示她的跑鞋漂亮。

scene.explanationZh: 句子保留個人重要性，沒有無根據的獎項。

options.en: A modest milestone can matter deeply to the person involved.
options.zh: 平實的里程碑也可以對當事人意義重大。

options.en: Pretty here describes the physical appearance of the event.
options.zh: 這裏的 pretty 是說活動外觀漂亮。

options.en: The phrase can sound conversational rather than ceremonial.
options.zh: 這個說法較像日常交談而非典禮用語。

contrast.explanationZh: pretty 在這裏加強程度，不是形容外貌。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「只是校內得獎，怎會是 a pretty big deal？」你怎樣回應？

options.en: It can be a pretty big deal to the pupil even if it is not nationally famous.
options.zh: 即使不是全國知名的獎項，對學生而言仍可以是件頗重要的事。

options.en: The phrase only applies to internationally famous events.
options.zh: 這個說法只適用於國際知名事件。

options.en: If an event is personal, it cannot be important.
options.zh: 事情若屬個人經歷，就不可能重要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 個人重要性不需要等同公眾知名度。

speaking.en: Getting the first acceptance letter was a pretty big deal to Noor after months of applications.
speaking.zh: 經過幾個月申請，收到第一封錄取信對努爾而言是件頗重要的事。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出是對誰重要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區合唱團的一名新成員練習半年後，首次獲安排獨唱一小段；觀眾只有二十人，但她很重視這機會。用一至兩句英文說明，不要誇稱她已成名。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出半年練習、首次獨唱對她個人重要，以及小型觀眾不等於成名。

examples.en: After six months of practice, singing her first solo is a pretty big deal to the new choir member, even with an audience of twenty.
examples.zh: 練習半年後，首次獨唱對這名合唱團新成員而言是件頗重要的事，即使觀眾只有二十人。

examples.en: Her first short solo is a pretty big deal to her after half a year in the community choir; the small audience does not make her famous.
examples.zh: 加入社區合唱團半年後，首次短暫獨唱對她而言是件頗重要的事；觀眾不多不代表她已成名。

takeaways.en: A pretty big deal can be personally important without being famous.
takeaways.zh: 一件頗重要的事可以只對當事人重要，而不必廣為人知。

takeaways.en: Calling something a pretty big deal does not mean it is famous.
takeaways.zh: 這裏的 pretty 是口語強調，不是「漂亮」。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Feel unnecessary or excluded in a group because no one gives you a role or includes you.
brief.meaningZh: 在群體中因沒有角色或未被納入而覺得自己多餘。
brief.grammar: Feel like a spare part; in the room is optional context, not part of the reusable unit.
brief.register: Informal social reflection: a host asks a co-host how to include a new guest who has been left outside the conversation.
brief.boundaryZh: 指人的主觀被排除感，不能因對方安靜就斷定；也不是機械零件。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不等於真的沒有價值；要留意是否缺乏參與機會。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認被晾在一旁的感受，並提出具體納入方法。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 77, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: No guest should feel like a spare part in the room.
sources.expression: a spare part in the room

listening.en: At dinner, the old friends discussed stories Ava did not know and never asked her a question. She began to feel like a spare part in the room.
listening.zh: 晚餐時，老朋友只談艾娃不知道的往事，也從沒問她問題。她開始覺得自己在房間裏像個多餘的人。
listening.promptZh: feel like a spare part 表示甚麼？

options.en: Ava felt left out and without a part in the conversation.
options.zh: 艾娃覺得自己被冷落，無法參與對話。

options.en: Ava was asked to repair a machine.
options.zh: 艾娃被要求維修機器。

options.en: Ava had chosen to tell the stories herself.
options.zh: 艾娃選擇親自講那些故事。

options.en: Ava knew every story well.
options.zh: 艾娃很熟悉每個故事。

listening.explanationZh: 別人沒有給她加入對話的機會。

reply.promptEn: Why did Ben leave the project meeting uneasy? Everyone assigned tasks among themselves before he arrived, then continued planning without asking what he could do.
reply.promptZh: （本為何不安地離開專題會議？他到達前大家已自行分配任務，之後繼續計劃，沒問他可做甚麼。）

options.en: Ben was not given a way to join the work.
options.zh: 本沒有獲得參與工作的機會。

options.en: The team overlooked his possible contribution.
options.zh: 團隊忽略了他可能作出的貢獻。

options.en: Ben felt like a spare part in the meeting.
options.zh: 本在會議中覺得自己多餘。

options.en: The planning left Ben without a role.
options.zh: 這次計劃令本沒有角色。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述缺乏參與角色；金句用 feel like a spare part。

scene.promptZh: 新同學坐在小組旁，別人不分派工作，也不回應他的提議。哪句最貼切？

options.en: He may feel like a spare part because nobody includes him.
options.zh: 沒有人讓他參與，他可能覺得自己多餘。

options.en: He must be unwilling to help.
options.zh: 他一定不願意幫忙。

options.en: He is literally a spare machine component.
options.zh: 他真的是一件備用機械零件。

scene.explanationZh: 有被排除的具體證據，但不能推測他不願幫忙。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以支持這個說法？

options.en: A guest is repeatedly ignored when she tries to join a conversation.
options.zh: 客人嘗試加入對話，卻一再被忽略。

options.en: A quiet guest is invited to help choose the music and happily accepts.
options.zh: 一名安靜客人獲邀選音樂，並開心接受。

options.en: A volunteer receives no task while the others plan together.
options.zh: 義工沒有獲分派任務，其他人一起計劃。

contrast.explanationZh: 安靜不等於被排除；這名客人有參與機會。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「她沒有說話，所以她一定覺得自己多餘。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Silence alone does not prove she feels like a spare part; ask whether she had a chance to join in.
options.zh: 單憑沉默不能證明；要看她有沒有參與機會。

options.en: Quiet people always feel excluded.
options.zh: 安靜的人一定覺得被排除。

options.en: Feeling excluded means the person has no value.
options.zh: 覺得被排除代表這人沒有價值。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需要參與機會的證據，不可只看沉默。

speaking.en: The organiser gave each newcomer a small role so no one would feel like a spare part during the workshop.
speaking.zh: 籌辦人給每位新來者一個小角色，讓大家在工作坊中不會覺得自己多餘。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出籌辦人如何避免冷落新來者。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：圖書館讀書會的舊成員一直談私下笑話，新成員想發言卻沒有機會。主持人打算請她先選下一本書。用一至兩句英文描述她可能的感受與改善方法，勿斷言她真的不喜歡讀書。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出私下笑話令她可能覺得被排除，以及主持人讓她選書。

examples.en: The newcomer may feel like a spare part when members trade private jokes; the host can invite her to choose the next book.
examples.zh: 成員互相講私下笑話時，新成員可能覺得自己多餘；主持人可請她選下一本書。

examples.en: Because she cannot enter the private conversation, the new member may feel like a spare part, so the host should give her a voice in the next book choice.
examples.zh: 因為她無法加入私下對話，新成員可能覺得自己多餘；主持人應讓她參與選下一本書。

takeaways.en: Feeling like a spare part describes exclusion, not a person’s worth.
takeaways.zh: 覺得自己多餘，說的是被排除的感受，不是人的價值。

takeaways.en: Someone can feel like a spare part when no one gives them a chance to join.
takeaways.zh: 要給新來者實際參與的機會。

brief.meaningEn: Gradually develop a comfortable natural flow without every moment being tightly directed.
brief.meaningZh: 逐漸形成舒適自然的進行節奏，毋須每刻嚴格指揮。
brief.grammar: An event, group or routine finds its own rhythm; possessive its agrees with the singular subject.
brief.register: Casual event planning: a neighbourhood host tells a volunteer that introductions may be guided, then conversation can develop naturally.
brief.boundaryZh: 自然節奏不等於完全沒有安排，也不保證人人自動融入。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是必須有音樂或固定拍子；是活動逐漸流暢。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分逐漸形成的活動節奏與失控或強行逐分鐘安排。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 77, row 11; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A relaxed gathering usually finds its own rhythm.

listening.en: The neighbours began with introductions, then small conversations grew without anyone directing each minute. The gathering found its own rhythm.
listening.zh: 鄰居先互相介紹，之後毋須有人逐分鐘指揮，大家便自然聊起來。聚會漸漸形成自己的節奏。
listening.promptZh: found its own rhythm 表示甚麼？

options.en: The gathering developed a comfortable flow.
options.zh: 聚會逐漸進行得自然順暢。

options.en: Someone played music at a fixed tempo.
options.zh: 有人以固定速度播放音樂。

options.en: Every minute was scripted in advance.
options.zh: 每一分鐘都預先寫好流程。

options.en: The host had no safety plan at all.
options.zh: 主人完全沒有安全安排。

listening.explanationZh: 對話自然延續，並非真正音樂節拍。

reply.promptEn: Why did the host stop announcing every conversation topic? After introductions, the guests began exchanging stories easily, and no one needed prompts to keep talking.
reply.promptZh: （主人為何不再逐一宣布話題？介紹過後，客人自然分享故事，毋須提示也能繼續交談。）

options.en: The guests were talking comfortably on their own.
options.zh: 客人已能自在交談。

options.en: Conversation no longer needed constant prompting.
options.zh: 交談不再需要不斷提示。

options.en: The gathering had found its own rhythm.
options.zh: 聚會已漸漸形成自然節奏。

options.en: Introductions helped conversation begin naturally.
options.zh: 介紹有助對話自然開始。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均描述引導後自然延續；金句用 found its own rhythm。

scene.promptZh: 工作坊開頭有簡短說明；之後小組自行輪流討論，毋須主持人逐句安排。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The workshop found its own rhythm after the introduction.
options.zh: 簡介過後，工作坊漸漸形成自然節奏。

options.en: The workshop became a music lesson.
options.zh: 工作坊變成音樂課。

options.en: The organiser had planned every utterance.
options.zh: 籌辦人安排了每句發言。

scene.explanationZh: 有起始安排，其後討論自然延續。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 find its own rhythm？

options.en: A team needs fewer prompts as members learn how to work together.
options.zh: 成員漸懂合作後，團隊較少需要提示。

options.en: A facilitator must interrupt and assign every sentence throughout.
options.zh: 引導員全程都須打斷並分派每句發言。

options.en: A new class begins awkwardly, then settles into an easy routine.
options.zh: 新班起初有點生硬，後來形成順暢慣例。

contrast.explanationZh: 全程仍靠逐句指揮，沒有自然形成的節奏。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「聚會自然順暢，就不需要照顧新來者。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: A gathering can find its own rhythm while the host still checks that newcomers can join in.
options.zh: 聚會可以形成自然節奏，主人仍要留意新來者能否參與。

options.en: Natural flow proves that every guest feels included.
options.zh: 自然順暢就證明每位客人都覺得被接納。

options.en: The phrase means the host must never prepare anything.
options.zh: 這個說法表示主人絕不能預先準備。

dialogue.explanationZh: 自然節奏不等於放棄照顧參與者。

speaking.en: After a short welcome, the reading circle found its own rhythm as members began responding to one another.
speaking.zh: 簡短歡迎後，讀書會成員開始互相回應，活動漸漸形成自然節奏。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出自然節奏如何形成。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區園藝小組首十分鐘由導師介紹工具，其後成員自行分工、互相請教；導師仍留意新手是否跟得上。用一至兩句英文說明活動如何進入自然節奏。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出首十分鐘有介紹、其後自行分工請教，以及導師仍照顧新手。

examples.en: After a ten-minute tool introduction, the gardening group found its own rhythm as members divided tasks and helped one another, while the tutor checked on beginners.
examples.zh: 十分鐘工具介紹後，園藝小組成員自行分工、互相幫忙，活動漸漸形成自然節奏；導師仍留意新手。

examples.en: The group found its own rhythm once members began sharing tasks and advice after the ten-minute tool introduction; the tutor still made sure beginners could keep up.
examples.zh: 十分鐘工具介紹後，成員開始分擔工作、互相請教，小組便漸漸形成自然節奏；導師仍確保新手跟得上。

takeaways.en: A group finds its own rhythm when interaction becomes natural.
takeaways.zh: 小組互動變得自然時，便可說它形成自己的節奏。

takeaways.en: A group can find its own rhythm while keeping sensible preparation.
takeaways.zh: 自然順暢仍可與適當準備及照顧新手並存。
